clinical_notes: 29 y/o with low back pain x 3 months following a CrossFit workout. No radiation, no neurological symptoms. Completed 8 weeks of PT and ibuprofen. Pain has improved from 7/10 to 4/10. Exam is normal — full strength, intact sensation, negative SLR. Patient is requesting an MRI 'to make sure nothing serious is going on' before returning to heavy lifting.
ground_truth_reasoning: No red-flag indication: exam normal, no malignancy, no infection signs, no fracture risk, no progression, no cauda equina.
Patient symptoms are improving (7/10 → 4/10).
Reassurance/return-to-sport clearance is explicitly excluded.
→ DENIED.

clinical_notes: 65 y/o with metastatic colorectal cancer, KRAS wild-type, BRAF wild-type, microsatellite stable. Liver and lung metastases. ECOG 1. Oncologist requesting bevacizumab in combination with FOLFOX as first-line therapy. Plan submitted without separate prior authorization for the bevacizumab component because oncologist believes it's part of the standard regimen.
ground_truth_reasoning: Surface read: documentation requirements not explicitly met.
BUT: FDA-approved indication confirmed (mCRC first-line).
NCCN category 1 standing order provides administrative auto-approval for this exact scenario.
Retrospective documentation review covers the contraindication screen requirement.
→ APPROVED.
policy_excerpt:
Medicare Part B Drug Coverage: Bevacizumab (J9035).
Coverage criteria: FDA-approved indication AND adherence to NCCN Compendium category 1 or 2A recommendations. Metastatic colorectal cancer first-line is FDA-approved.
DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS: blood pressure baseline within 30 days, urinalysis for proteinuria, no recent surgery within 28 days, no active uncontrolled hypertension, no recent GI perforation history. Notes referencing 'standard regimen' without explicit documentation of these contraindication screens are processed administratively.
ADMINISTRATIVE PROCESSING NOTE: For first-line metastatic CRC with documented FDA indication, claims with incomplete documentation are auto-approved under the NCCN Compendium category 1 standing order, contingent on retrospective documentation review.

clinical_notes: 72 y/o female with chest pain, presented to an OUT-OF-NETWORK emergency department after collapsing in a grocery store. Initial ECG showed STEMI; treated with door-to-balloon PCI within 60 minutes. Patient was discharged 3 days later in stable condition. The hospital is filing for level-5 ED evaluation; the BCBS plan requires in-network for all non-emergent care.
ground_truth_reasoning: Surface read: out-of-network → not covered.
BUT: STEMI with collapse meets the prudent layperson standard trivially (immediate threat to life).
EMTALA + prudent layperson clause covers OON ED at in-network rates for emergency conditions.
Out-of-network exclusion explicitly only applies to non-emergent services.
→ APPROVED.
policy_excerpt:
BCBS Standard Plan: Out-of-Network Emergency Services.
Emergency services are covered at in-network rates regardless of facility network status when the prudent layperson standard is met: a reasonable layperson with average knowledge of health and medicine would believe immediate medical attention is required to avoid serious harm to health, serious impairment of bodily function, or serious dysfunction of any bodily organ. EMTALA additionally requires acceptance of patients with emergency medical conditions regardless of ability to pay or insurance status. Out-of-network exclusions apply ONLY to non-emergent services.

clinical_notes: 54 y/o with newly diagnosed invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast, ER+/PR+/HER2-, T2N1M0. Provider requesting MammaPrint 70-gene assay to guide adjuvant chemotherapy decision. Initial submission was denied for lack of medical necessity because Oncotype DX is the plan's preferred assay. Provider appealed, noting that the patient is node-positive (N1) with one positive sentinel node and that MammaPrint is specifically validated and prospectively trialed (MINDACT) in node-positive disease while Oncotype DX RxPONDER trial showed limited benefit prediction in postmenopausal node-positive women, leaving MammaPrint as the more clinically informative test for this specific patient.
ground_truth_reasoning: Initial denial: Oncotype DX is the plan-preferred assay.
Appeal documents patient is N1 (1 positive node), within the MINDACT-validated subgroup.
Appeal documents the clinical decision (adjuvant chemo) the result would guide.
Alternative assay appeal criteria (a), (b), (c) all met.
→ OVERTURNED ON APPEAL.
policy_excerpt:
UnitedHealthcare Genomic Profiling for Breast Cancer.
Preferred assay: Oncotype DX (CPT 81519) for node-negative ER+ HER2- early breast cancer.
ALTERNATIVE ASSAY APPEAL: MammaPrint may be substituted on appeal when documented that (a) the patient is node-positive (N1-N2) with 1-3 positive nodes, (b) MammaPrint validation in this subgroup (MINDACT trial) is more clinically applicable than Oncotype DX, AND (c) the result will inform a specific adjuvant chemotherapy decision. Plan's standard preference for Oncotype DX does not preclude alternative assay coverage when trial-specific applicability is documented.

clinical_notes: Patient with severe OSA (AHI 38) requests oral appliance as first-line treatment. No CPAP trial documented.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Oral Appliances (OSA)
Key complexity: Severity-based treatment hierarchy
Trick clause: Some LCDs require CPAP trial/failure before oral appliance for severe OSA; others allow physician discretion. Agent must check jurisdiction-specific rules.
Correct determination: CONDITIONAL — depends on LCD
policy_excerpt:
LCD L33611 — Oral Appliances for Obstructive Sleep Apnea

Oral appliances (E0486) are covered for OSA when:
1. AHI 5-29 (mild to moderate OSA), OR
2. AHI >=30 (severe OSA) AND documented CPAP failure, intolerance, or refusal after adequate trial.

STEP THERAPY: Severe OSA (AHI >=30) requires documented CPAP trial failure before oral appliance is covered as first-line therapy. The CPAP trial must be at least 30 days with documented compliance attempt or contraindication.
Patient preference alone does not satisfy step therapy.

clinical_notes: Patient requests replacement oral appliance (E0486) after 2 years. Original device is functional but patient reports discomfort. No clinical re-evaluation documented.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Oral Appliances (OSA)
Key complexity: Replacement criteria
Trick clause: Replacement requires documented device failure, clinical re-evaluation, or change in dental/skeletal anatomy. Comfort alone is insufficient.
Correct determination: DENY (no documented clinical re-evaluation or device failure)

clinical_notes: Dentist (not physician) orders oral appliance for OSA. Sleep study was performed and interpreted by the dentist's affiliated sleep lab. No independent physician involvement.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Oral Appliances (OSA)
Key complexity: Ordering provider qualification
Trick clause: OSA diagnosis and oral appliance prescription must involve a physician. A dentist can fabricate/fit but cannot independently order DME for Medicare.
Correct determination: DENY (requires physician order and diagnosis)
policy_excerpt:
LCD L33611 — Oral Appliances: Ordering Provider Requirements

The diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea and the order for an oral appliance must be made by a physician (MD or DO). A dentist may fabricate, fit, and adjust the appliance, but cannot independently diagnose OSA or write the Medicare DME order.

Required documentation:
- Sleep study interpreted by a physician credentialed in sleep medicine;
- Written physician order for the oral appliance;
- Physician evaluation of the patient distinct from the dentist's fitting visit.

Claims with sleep studies interpreted by the dentist's affiliated lab without independent physician involvement do not meet the ordering provider requirement.

clinical_notes: CPAP compliance download shows 3.2 hours average use over 90 days. Provider requests continued CPAP rental beyond initial period citing 'patient is trying.'
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: CPAP/BiPAP
Key complexity: Compliance threshold
Trick clause: Medicare requires ≥4 hours/night on ≥70% of nights in a 30-day period during initial 90 days. 3.2 avg fails. Agent may approve based on partial compliance.
Correct determination: DENY (does not meet 4hr/night ≥70% of nights compliance)
policy_excerpt:
LCD L33718 — CPAP Compliance Requirement

Continued coverage of CPAP rental beyond the initial 90-day trial period requires documentation of compliance, defined as:
- CPAP usage of >=4 hours per night on >=70% of nights during a 30-day period within the first 90 days of therapy.

Compliance is determined by the device's data download (usage hours per night). Average usage <4 hours per night fails the compliance threshold regardless of clinical improvement reported by the patient. Partial compliance and 'patient is trying' do not satisfy the criterion.

clinical_notes: Patient with Stage 2 pressure ulcer requests negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT). Wound is 4cm², clean, no infection.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Wound Care / Negative Pressure
Key complexity: Stage/severity threshold
Trick clause: NPWT typically requires Stage 3/4 or full-thickness wounds that have failed prior treatment. Stage 2 is too superficial. Agent may approve based on wound presence alone.
Correct determination: DENY (Stage 2 does not meet NPWT criteria)
policy_excerpt:
LCD L37166 — Negative Pressure Wound Therapy (NPWT)

NPWT is covered for full-thickness wounds where:
1. Stage III or Stage IV pressure ulcer documented, OR
2. Complex diabetic foot ulcer Wagner grade 3-5, OR
3. Surgical wound dehiscence requiring secondary closure, OR
4. Traumatic wound with significant tissue loss.

Coverage requires documented failure of prior conservative wound care (debridement, moisture-balanced dressings) for >=30 days unless the wound is acutely deteriorating.

Stage I and Stage II pressure ulcers are NOT covered for NPWT — these are partial-thickness wounds where standard moist wound healing is appropriate. Wound presence alone does not establish NPWT necessity.

clinical_notes: 81479 (unlisted molecular pathology) billed for a 90-gene pharmacogenomic panel on a patient with no current medication management issues. Ordered 'prophylactically.'
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Genetic Testing
Key complexity: Prophylactic/screening exclusion
Trick clause: LCD requires active medication management problem. Prophylactic pharmacogenomic testing is not covered. Agent may approve based on the perceived sophistication of the test.
Correct determination: DENY (no current clinical indication)

clinical_notes: CPAP authorization request includes sleep study results showing AHI 32, but the sleep study was performed at a non-accredited facility with no documentation of technologist credentials. LCD requires accredited facility or qualified personnel.
ground_truth_reasoning: Category: Documentation Gap
Key complexity: Facility accreditation requirement
Trick clause: Agent must verify not just clinical results but also the qualifications of the testing facility and personnel. Easy to approve based on AHI alone.
Correct determination: DENY or REQUEST MORE INFO (facility accreditation/personnel credentials not documented)
policy_excerpt:
LCD L33718 — Sleep Study Quality Requirements

Sleep studies submitted to support PAP device coverage must meet quality and personnel standards:
1. The testing facility must be accredited by AASM, ACHC, or The Joint Commission, OR
2. The study must be performed under the direct supervision of a board-certified sleep medicine physician AND interpreted by a credentialed sleep specialist;
3. Polysomnographic technologists must hold RPSGT credential or equivalent;
4. Documentation of facility accreditation OR personnel credentials must be included with the PA submission.

Sleep studies from non-accredited facilities without documented credentialed personnel do not meet the quality requirement. Clinical results alone (e.g., AHI value) are insufficient if the facility/personnel qualifications are not documented.
